description: LEAD GENERATION FROM BUYING SIGNALS: prospects showing a reason to buy now. One on-demand search runs a handful of public lookups and returns COMPANIES, one row per company, each with its OWN WEBSITE (from its job board, the ad, the article, its channel, or its name confirmed by its homepage; a company with none is left out) and the post, ad or page that is the signal (link, date, why it matched). SIGNAL TYPES: new_ads_meta, new_ads_linkedin (companies running new ads), hiring (companies hiring for a role), funding, web (any web search), posts_reddit, posts_threads, posts_tiktok, posts_youtube (people asking, or complaining about a competitor). When the buyer is a business, individual posters come back apart under people. GIVE IT description (who the user sells to), or keywords and competitors, or signals [{ type, query }]; an unknown type is refused with the list. Filters country, size, industry and uses (ad pixels on the site) drop rows the company's own site contradicts; sorted by fit, then recency; a company already in the brand's email leads or do-not-email list is marked. PAID: about 1 credit per lookup (up to 8; planning from a description adds a small writing cost), never more than maxCredits (default 10): it stops at the budget and names what it did not run. Reading the websites is free. DryRun:true prices it. A failed lookup is "could not read", never "no leads". Find_leads({ searchId, id }) returns one row in full, free, for 30 minutes (nothing is stored). SaveAs keeps the search for saved_lead_searches; search_companies finds companies by industry rather than by signal. Works with nothing connected.

audience.description: business | consumer (default: read from the description); business lists individual posters apart under people

competitors.description: competitor names, to find people asking for an alternative (up to 3)

country.description: 2-letter country; a company whose own site places it elsewhere is left out

days.description: how recent the signal must be, 1 to 90 (default 30)

description.description: who the user sells to, in plain words ("dental clinics in Texas that run ads")

dryRun.description: true = the price and the plan only; nothing looked up or charged

expected_credits.description: the get_cost price; refused unbilled if the live price differs

get_cost.description: true: return the price only; nothing runs or bills

id.description: a lead id from that search, such as L3

idempotency_key.description: chosen once, resent unchanged on retries: the same key never buys twice

industry.description: any words ("marketing agency", "dental clinic"); a company whose own site does not read as it is left out

keywords.description: words a buyer or their ads would use (up to 5)

language.description: the language to write planned queries in

maxCredits.description: HARD budget in credits (default 10, max 60): the search stops before passing it

saveAs.description: a name: keep this search so saved_lead_searches can re-run it for new companies only

searchId.description: with id: read one lead of an earlier search in full (free)

signals.description: explicit lookups (up to 8), each billed; replaces the automatic plan

query.description: any free-text query for that source

type.description: new_ads_meta | new_ads_linkedin | posts_reddit | posts_threads | posts_tiktok | posts_youtube | hiring | funding | web

size.description: staff range ("2-50", "200+") or small / mid-size / enterprise; a company whose site says otherwise is left out

types.description: limit the automatic plan to these signal types

uses.description: tags its homepage must carry: meta_pixel, google_ads, tiktok_pixel, linkedin_insight, pinterest_tag, snap_pixel, reddit_pixel, x_pixel, microsoft_uet, google_analytics, shopify, woocommerce, wordpress, webflow, wix, squarespace, hubspot, klaviyo, intercom, stripe, app_store, google_play

name: find_leads
title: Find leads from buying signals
